clue.text: A revolutionary device for the traveller

definitions.text: A revolutionary device for the traveller

blocks.note: surface reading: an invention that overturns the old order, as if politically radical
setter's reading: revolutionary simply means turning round and round, as the thing under a cart or car does

explanation.surface: A traveller is offered some radical new gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics or a breakthrough, but here it is literal: the device revolves. The answer is WHEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel rotates on its axle and carries every vehicle a traveller rides in.

clue.text: Flighty creatures have fun in clubs

indicators.note: whatever has something holds it, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: woods are golf clubs with large heads
a lark is a bit of fun

explanation.surface: Frivolous people enjoy themselves at nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests fickle, but it means able to fly: the creatures are birds, woodlarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlarks are small songbirds of the lark family, and birds are creatures of flight.

clue.text: The more mature tree?

blocks.note: first meaning: older of two
second meaning: a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking which tree is older, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder is the comparative of old, and also the name of the shrub Sambucus.

clue.text: Painting places and characters in a different way

indicators.note: arranged in a different way means put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist depicts locations and people unconventionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in the picture; it means the letters of the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting depicting a view of countryside or natural scenery.

clue.text: A top man quietly staying in

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly
someone resident is living, staying, in a place

explanation.surface: An important figure keeps a low profile by remaining indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation, the person at the very top.

clue.text: The little page with an awful longing for flamboyance

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
taken as written
an ache is a painful yearning

explanation.surface: A young page boy pines terribly to be showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' tells you to shorten page to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is a dashing, stylish confidence, a flamboyant manner.

clue.text: When they close down viewing's at an end

definitions.text: When they close down viewing's at an end

blocks.clueFragment: When they close down viewing's at an end
blocks.note: surface reading: when some cinemas or channels shut down, there is nothing left to watch
setter's reading: they literally come down and close, and then a person sees nothing

explanation.surface: Once the broadcasters shut up shop, there is nothing left to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like television closedown; the things that close downward are EYELIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelids are the folds of skin that lower over the eyes, shutting off sight.

clue.text: A block-house offers cold comfort

blocks.note: surface reading: a military blockhouse is a grim, unwelcoming shelter
setter's reading: a house literally built of blocks, of snow, whose comfort is cold indeed

explanation.surface: A fortified outpost is a bleak place to shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A blockhouse is a small fort, and 'cold comfort' means little consolation; both are literal for an IGLOO.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome dwelling built from blocks of packed snow.

clue.text: Work in secret to produce mince-pies on time

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Bake festive pastries on schedule, in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince-pies' looks like one word, the Christmas pastry; mince is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is spying, covert work to gather secret information.

clue.text: Alcoholic liquor that's divine in trifle

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: to toy with is to trifle
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a divine

explanation.surface: A heavenly boozy dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a clergyman; DD is the degree a learned divine holds. Trifle is a British dessert soaked in sherry, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, sugar and water, so an alcoholic mixed liquor.

clue.text: The regulation of Israeli capital invested in munitions

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another
a capital is a head letter, so only the opening letter of the word before it is wanted

blocks.note: ordnance is military supplies, especially artillery and ammunition
the first letter of Israeli

explanation.surface: A rule about money from Jerusalem being sunk into the arms trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Israeli capital' looks like Jerusalem or shekels, but it is just the capital letter I, placed inside ORDNANCE to make ORDINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or rule, especially a municipal by-law.

clue.text: Made rapid progress when given guidance about work

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: someone given guidance was led
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone's career advanced quickly once they had a mentor for their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides, so loped means covered ground quickly.

clue.text: Girl embraces right little beast in Madagascar!

indicators.note: whoever embraces something holds it within their arms

blocks.note: Lois is a girl's name
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A girl on holiday in Madagascar hugs a small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorises actually live in South and South-East Asia; the Madagascan cousins are lemurs, so the definition is loose, as the exclamation mark half admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A loris is a small, slow-moving nocturnal primate with huge eyes, a relative of the lemurs.

clue.text: The footman's function

blocks.note: surface reading: the duties of a liveried servant who opens doors and waits at table
setter's reading: a foot man is a professional who treats feet, and his function is that medical work

explanation.surface: What a household servant in livery is employed to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A footman is a servant, but split it as foot-man and he becomes a specialist in feet: CHIROPODY, the work of a chiropodist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiropody is the treatment of foot ailments, the trade of a chiropodist or podiatrist.

clue.text: Put back some stuff — delicate stuff

blocks.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a kind of stuff
lace is a fine, delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Someone returns some material, the fragile kind, to where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is an old word for cloth; rep is a heavy corded upholstery fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to return it to its proper position.

clue.text: Schemes include a tin specially designed for fruit

indicators.note: something specially designed is given a fresh shape, so these letters get a new order
to include something is to take it inside

blocks.note: plans are schemes
the letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: Plans call for a custom-made can to hold fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantains are starchy banana-like fruits, usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: Set wrong by minor official

indicators.note: something put wrong is out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of set, to be rearranged
a ward is a minor placed under the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: A junior functionary gets something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor official' reads as one phrase, but minor is wordplay and official alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an official who manages arrangements, as at a race meeting or in a household.

clue.text: No longer sadly thinking the cost is unreasonable

definitions.note: a clause describing something rather than an adjective; it reads as 'such that the cost is unreasonable'

blocks.note: ex means former, no longer so
pensive means lost in wistful thought

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped brooding still feels the price is too high.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expensive costs a lot, more than seems fair or reasonable to pay.

clue.text: Pull down Diana's cloak

blocks.note: Di is short for Diana, with the possessive s
a mantle is a loose sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: Someone tugs Diana's cape down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a structure is to take it apart, demolishing or pulling it down.

clue.text: Children must retain respect for these plants

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the first piece holds the second within it

blocks.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical usage
awe is deep respect mixed with wonder

explanation.surface: Children are told to keep their regard for certain plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are marine algae, often thought of loosely as plants growing in the sea.

clue.text: Its operators are forever scraping the bottom

definitions.text: Its operators are forever scraping the bottom

blocks.clueFragment: Its operators are forever scraping the bottom
blocks.note: surface reading: a business run by people always reaching for the lowest standard, scraping the barrel
setter's reading: the vessel's crew literally scoop mud from the bed of a river or harbour

explanation.surface: A firm whose managers always stoop to the lowest standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraping the bottom' suggests scraping the barrel, desperate measures; here it is literal for a DREDGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a vessel or machine that scoops silt from the bed of a waterway.

clue.text: Hold back a note and the newspapers will be after it!

indicators.note: coming after it means this part is placed behind the earlier one

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Suppress a memo, or the journalists will come hunting for it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will be after it' sounds like reporters chasing a story; it only says where the second piece goes. Re is the sol-fa note, as in do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to restrain or suppress, keeping a feeling or fact in check.

clue.text: Will soldiers provide the answer?

blocks.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
to solve is to find the answer

explanation.surface: A question: can the army sort this out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as the future auxiliary, but it is the noun, determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firm determination, strength of will to carry something through.

clue.text: Unequalled footballers wanting a game?

blocks.note: first meaning: without a rival or peer
second meaning, read whimsically: players who lack a fixture are without one

explanation.surface: Peerless players are left without a fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the word split as MATCH-LESS: footballers with no match. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means having no equal, too good to be matched by any rival.

clue.text: Pined for personal transport

blocks.note: first meaning: ... about, was listless and miserable
second meaning: a low-powered motorbike for one rider

explanation.surface: Someone longed for a vehicle of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pined for' runs together as yearned, but 'for' only links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mope means to be dejected and listless; a moped is a small motor-assisted bicycle.

clue.text: Beaten over church problem

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top

blocks.note: hit means struck, beaten
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A defeat over some church issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag, a temporary difficulty that holds things up.

clue.text: Such antelope may be seen in many a land

indicators.note: what may be seen within a phrase is sitting inside its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Antelope of this type can be spotted across many countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Assemble for a service

blocks.note: taken as written
Mass is the Eucharistic church service

explanation.surface: A congregation gathers for worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect a large quantity together.

clue.text: Object to pin being misused

indicators.note: something misused is put to the wrong purpose, so these letters are wrongly arranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a pin is being used wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a verb, to protest, but it is the noun: aim or purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of something is its purpose or aim, as in 'what is the point?'.

clue.text: Play about animosity shown by one against a worker

blocks.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
I is the Roman numeral one
v, versus, means against
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A drama about resentment in the workplace, one person set against a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a stage drama with 'about' meaning concerning; together they are the verb phrase, to fool around.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to go around seeking pleasure, roaming about frivolously.

clue.text: The underworld fill up free

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
to charge is to load or fill, as a glass or a gun

explanation.surface: Gangsters stock up on something they got for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner or patient is to release them, setting them free.

clue.text: Follow directions and take legal action

blocks.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
to sue is to bring a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Obey instructions, then go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards as a result, so to follow on.
